grh_0fa7e5842967703f8eeb.title: Canine Justice
paragraphs: Young Teddy Douglas is devoted to Laddie, the family's discharged K-9 Corps dog whose wartime training makes him far more than an ordinary pet. Exploring an abandoned house that neighborhood children consider haunted, Teddy discovers a wanted jewel thief hiding there with stolen property. The fugitive catches the boy, ties him up and plans to leave him helpless while he escapes. Teddy warns that Laddie will come when called, and when the armed criminal threatens the dog, Laddie attacks and subdues him badly enough for the police to capture him. The thief survives and is identified as a man wanted in several cities, making Teddy eligible for a substantial reward. When officials then discuss destroying Laddie because he attacked a human being, Dr. Christian insists the dog used the training given him in war to save a child's life and help bring a dangerous criminal to justice, and vows to fight any attempt to punish him for it.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on August 15, 1945. It is listed as episode 351 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Bob Anderson as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 24 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_0fde923b3bf23e176698.title: Bachelor Mother
paragraphs: Department-store clerk Polly Parish finds an abandoned baby and is mistaken for its mother, a misunderstanding that follows her back to work when the foundling home and her employers decide she must accept responsibility for the child. Store heir David Merlin becomes personally involved in Polly's predicament and gradually falls in love with her, while his father becomes convinced the baby is David's own secret son. By the time Polly can explain that she is not the mother at all, David no longer cares: he publicly claims the child as his, declares that he and Polly are marrying that night, and only then learns she still has one final surprise about the baby's true parentage.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Lucille Ball, Robert Cummings, Frank Nelson, Arthur Q. Bryan, and Garson Kanin. The surviving recording runs about 60 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.0ee8343bca2245d4|Chesterfield]] and [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]].

grh_0fc05edd4b6fa2fa21d8.title: Puff
paragraphs: Young Ted was blinded during a bombing in France that killed his family, and he insists that his beloved white poodle Puff still visits and guides him even though no one else can see the dog. X-rays reveal a treatable brain injury, but after successful surgery Ted still cannot see, leading Dr. Christian to suspect that fear and grief are blocking the recovery. When Ted's father, previously reported missing in action, unexpectedly returns, Ted finally uses his eyes and recognizes him. The father then tells how a mysterious white poodle led him safely through a German minefield, eerily echoing Ted's stories of Puff and leaving the dog's true nature unexplained.

The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_0f79a329af2c62b275ea.title: Son of the Chief
paragraphs: Former cavalryman Magoon Fraley seeks revenge on retired Colonel Duncan by rustling his cattle and planting evidence to blame Sioux chief Swift Antelope, while hiding the fact that years earlier he kidnapped Duncan's young son and left the boy to be raised among the Sioux; Cisco exposes Fraley's scheme, captures him, reveals that Swift Antelope's adopted son Billy is Duncan's missing child, and helps end the old feud without forcing the boy to abandon the chief who raised him.
